I’m sorry you’re going through this. You can often get more than one kind of help at the same time, but it depends on the programs and on the rules in the county where you live. Below is a simple guide to the most common California assistance programs, what you need to qualify, what you’ll have to turn in, and how to apply.  

---

## 1. Unemployment Insurance (UI)  
**What it is:** Money paid for a few weeks while you look for a new job.  

**Who can get it:**  
* You worked in California and earned enough wages in the “base period” (usually the first four of the last five quarters you worked).  
* You are able and available to work, and you are actively looking for a job.  

**How to apply:**  
1. Go to **ui.ca.gov** or call the UI claims line.  
2. Create an account, fill out the online claim, and answer the work‑search questions each week.  

**Documents you may need:**  
* Your last employer’s name, address, and dates you worked.  
* Your most recent pay stub or W‑2.  

**Timeline:**  
* First payment usually arrives within 2‑3 weeks after you file the claim, if everything is correct.  

**Can you get other help at the same time?** Yes. UI does **not** stop you from applying for CalWORKs, SNAP, or Medi‑Cal, but each program will look at your UI income when they decide how much you may receive.

---

## 2. CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids) – Cash Aid  
**What it is:** Monthly cash assistance for families with children (or adults with a disability) who have low or no income.  

**Who can get it:**  
* You live in California, have a child under 18 (or a disabled adult), and meet income‑and‑asset limits that vary by county.  
* You must be willing to work or take part in a job‑training plan (unless you’re exempt).  

**How to apply:**  
1. Contact your **County Human Services Agency (HSA)** – you can find the phone number on the county website or call 1‑877‑847‑3663.  
2. Fill out the **CalWORKs Application** (online in many counties, or in person).  

**Documents you may need:**  
* Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).  
* Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or mortgage statement).  
* Birth certificates for each child.  
* Recent pay stubs, bank statements, or any other income proof.  

**Timeline:**  
* After you submit a complete application, the county must decide within **30 days** (or 45 days if you’re applying for a “hardship” case).  

**Can you get other help at the same time?** Yes. CalWORKs can be combined with UI, SNAP, Medi‑Cal, and housing assistance. The amount you receive may be reduced based on the UI benefits you are already getting.

---

## 3. SNAP (CalFresh) – Food Benefits  
**What it is:** Monthly benefits loaded onto an EBT card to buy groceries.  

**Who can get it:**  
* Anyone who lives in California, has low income, and meets the county’s income‑and‑asset limits (these limits differ a bit by county).  

**How to apply:**  
1. Apply online at **getcalfresh.org**, by phone (1‑877‑847‑3663), or at your local HSA office.  
2. Fill out the **CalFresh Application** and answer the interview questions.  

**Documents you may need:**  
* Photo ID.  
* Proof of income (pay stubs, UI award letter, unemployment benefits, etc.).  
* Proof of residence.  

**Timeline:**  
* The county must make a decision within **30 days** of receiving a complete application.  

**Can you get other help at the same time?** Yes. SNAP can be received together with UI, CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal, and housing assistance. Your UI or CalWORKs income will be counted when the county calculates your SNAP benefit amount.

---

## 4. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid) – Health Coverage  
**What it is:** Free or low‑cost health insurance for low‑income Californians.  

**Who can get it:**  
* Anyone who lives in California, meets income limits (which vary by household size and county), and is a U.S. citizen, national, or qualified immigrant.  

**How to apply:**  
1. Apply online at **CoveredCA.com**, by phone (1‑800‑300‑1506), or at a local HSA office.  

**Documents you may need:**  
* Photo ID.  
* Proof of income (pay stubs, UI award, etc.).  
* Proof of residence.  

**Timeline:**  
* Usually you’ll get a decision within **2‑4 weeks** after a complete application.  

**Can you get other help at the same time?** Absolutely. Medi‑Cal works with UI, CalWORKs, SNAP, and housing programs. Your UI or CalWORKs income will affect the Medi‑Cal cost‑share, but you can still be enrolled.

---

## 5. Housing Assistance (Section 8, Public Housing, Emergency Rental Assistance)  
**What it is:** Help paying rent or getting a voucher for a private apartment.  

**Who can get it:**  
* Low‑income households that meet the county’s income limits (often 30‑50 % of the area median income).  

**How to apply:**  
1. Contact your **County Housing Authority** or the local **Public Housing Agency (PHA)**.  
2. Fill out the specific application (many counties have online portals).  

**Documents you may need:**  
* Photo ID.  
* Proof of income (pay stubs, UI award, CalWORKs award, etc.).  
* Proof of residence and lease.  

**Timeline:**  
* Wait times vary a lot—some counties have waiting lists that can be months or years. Emergency Rental Assistance often has a faster turnaround (a few weeks) if you qualify.  

**Can you get other help at the same time?** Yes. You can receive UI, CalWORKs, SNAP, and Medi‑Cal while you’re on a housing program. All income is considered when the housing agency decides how much rent you must pay.

---

## Putting It All Together

2. **Apply for UI first** (if you haven’t already) because the UI award is needed for the other applications.

1. **Gather your documents**  
   - Social Security number  
   - Driver’s license or state ID (or a copy of it)  
   - Most recent pay stubs or a “last employer notice” that shows your wages and dates of employment  
   - Bank account number (for direct deposit)

   - Go to **[UI Online (UI Online portal)](https://edd.ca.gov/Unemployment/UI_Online.htm)** or call the EDD at **1‑800‑300‑5616**.  
   - The first claim is free and can be done any day, any time.  

3. **Answer the questionnaire**  
   - You’ll be asked about your last job, why you left, and whether you’re looking for work. Answer honestly—any mistake can delay payment.  

4. **Submit your “Continuing Claim” each week**  
   - After the first claim is approved, you must log in every week (or call) to tell the EDD if you worked any hours, earned any money, or had any job offers.  

5. **Wait for the first payment**  
   - The EDD usually processes a claim within **about 2 weeks**. The first payment comes after the “waiting week” (the first week you claim, which is unpaid).  

---

| Tip | Why it helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Apply right away** | The sooner you file, the sooner the waiting week ends and the sooner you start getting money. |
| **Report all earnings** | If you pick up part‑time work, you can still get a reduced benefit. Not reporting can stop your payments. |
| **Look for “partial benefits”** | Even a few hours of work can keep you eligible for a smaller weekly amount, which adds up. |
| **Ask about extensions** | If the state declares a “COVID‑19 or other emergency” extension, you may qualify for extra weeks. |
| **Check for “training” or “re‑employment” programs** | Some counties offer job‑training vouchers that can be combined with UI. |
| **Keep good records** | Save any job‑search logs, interview confirmations, and emails. The EDD may ask for proof. |

Even if UI is your main focus, you may qualify for other California programs that can ease rent, food, or health‑care costs while you’re looking for work.

| Program | What it covers | How to apply |

| Action | Approximate time frame |
|--------|------------------------|

| **First payment** | After the waiting week + processing (about 3‑4 weeks from filing) |

| **Other programs (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, etc.)** | Usually 2‑4 weeks after you submit a complete application, but it varies by county |

---

## 7. County‑Specific Note  

Every California county runs its own **Human Services Agency** and may have slightly different forms, office hours, or extra local programs. After you file UI, you can also call your **County Employment Development Department (EDD) office** to ask about any county‑specific resources or deadlines.

---

### Quick Checklist for You  

- [ ] Gather ID, SSN, recent pay stubs, bank info  
- [ ] File UI claim online or by phone today  
- [ ] Set a reminder to file your weekly continuing claim every Friday  
- [ ] Look up your county’s Human Services Agency website for CalWORKs, CalFresh, and ERA applications  
- [ ] Keep a notebook of every job‑search activity (applications, interviews, contacts)

**You’re not alone.** The state has many tools to help you while you search for a new job. If you get stuck, call the EDD at **1‑800‑300‑5616** (they have a TTY line at **1‑800‑815‑9387**) or visit your local County Human Services office for in‑person help.

**I’m sorry you’ve been laid off.  Below is a simple guide to places that can help you look for a new job in California and how they can link you to other benefits.**  

---

## 1. Where to start looking for a job  

| Service | What it does | How to get started | What you’ll need |
|---------|--------------|--------------------|------------------|
| **CalJOBS (the state job‑search website)** | Lists thousands of open jobs, lets you upload a resume, and matches you with jobs that fit your skills. | Go to **www.caljobs.ca.gov** and create a free account. | A valid email address, your work history (dates, job titles, duties), and a basic resume (you can use the “resume builder” on the site). |
| **Local One‑Stop Career Centers** (run by the California Workforce Development Board) | In‑person help: job‑search workshops, resume help, interview practice, and referrals to employers. | Find the nearest center at **www.caljobs.ca.gov/centers** or call 1‑800‑555‑5555. | Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport), Social Security number, recent pay stubs or a lay‑off notice, and a copy of your resume (if you have one). |
| **California Employment Development Department (EDD) – Unemployment Insurance (UI) office** | Helps you file for UI benefits *and* can refer you to job‑search resources. | File a UI claim online at **edd.ca.gov/Unemployment** or call the UI line (1‑800‑300‑5616). | Your last employer’s name, dates of work, last pay stub, and your driver’s license or ID number. |
| **County Workforce Development Board (WDB)** | Each county runs its own job‑placement programs, training grants, and sometimes “quick‑hire” events. | Look up your county’s WDB website (search “[Your County] Workforce Development Board”). | Same as the One‑Stop Center – ID, SSN, and proof of recent employment. |
| **Community‑Based Organizations (CBOs) & Non‑profits** (e.g., Goodwill, United Way, local churches) | Offer job‑search classes, computer training, and sometimes direct connections to employers. | Call your local United Way (211) or visit a nearby Goodwill job‑center. | Photo ID and any certificates from past training (if you have them). |

### How they connect to benefits  

* **UI (Unemployment Insurance)** – When you file a UI claim, the EDD will ask you to **register on CalJOBS** and to **search for work each week**. That satisfies the “work‑search” requirement for UI.  
* **Training & Education Grants** – Many One‑Stop Centers and county WDBs can enroll you in **California’s Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) training**. If you qualify, the training can be paid for while you receive UI.  
* **Health Coverage** – If your UI runs out, the staff can help you apply for **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid) or **Covered California** health plans.  

---

## 2. Basic eligibility for the main programs  

| Program | Who can apply? |
|---------|----------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | You must have earned enough wages in the “base period” (the first four of the last five quarters you worked) and be unemployed through no fault of your own (a lay‑off qualifies). |
| **CalJOBS registration** | Anyone looking for work in California. No income test. |
| **One‑Stop Career Center services** | Residents of the county where the center is located. No income test. |
| **WIOA training** | Must be a UI claimant, a low‑income adult, or a dislocated worker. The exact income limits can differ by county, so the center will check your situation. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Income must be at or below 138 % of the federal poverty level, but there are special rules for people receiving UI. The county will verify your income. |

*Remember: each county may have small differences in how they verify income or work history, so the staff will tell you exactly what they need.*

---

## 3. Step‑by‑step checklist  

1. **File for UI right away** (within 1 week of your lay‑off).  
   * Go to the EDD website or call the UI line.  
   * Keep a copy of your lay‑off notice or a letter from your former boss.  

2. **Create a CalJOBS account** (you’ll need it for UI work‑search proof).  
   * Fill out the “profile” with your work history and skills.  
   * Upload a simple resume (the site can help you build one).  

3. **Visit your local One‑Stop Career Center** (or call to set an appointment).  
   * Bring: photo ID, Social Security card, recent pay stub or lay‑off notice, and your resume.  
   * Ask for:  
     * Resume review  
     * Interview practice  
     * List of local employers hiring now  
     * Information on any training programs (WIOA, apprenticeships, community‑college courses).  

4. **Apply for any training or education you need** (if you want new skills).  
   * The Center will help you fill out the WIOA application.  
   * If approved, you can start training while still getting UI benefits.  

5. **Check for other help** (Medi‑Cal, SNAP, CalWORKs, etc.).  
   * The Center or the county’s Human Services Agency can run a quick “benefits eligibility” check for you.  

6. **Keep a weekly work‑search log** (required for UI).  
   * Log each job you applied for, the date, and the employer’s name.  
   * You can do this directly in CalJOBS, which will automatically record it for UI.  

---

## 4. Documents you’ll usually need  

| Document | Why it’s needed |
|----------|-----------------|
| **Photo ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) | Proves you live in California and verifies your identity. |
| **Social Security number** | Required for UI, Medi‑Cal, and most benefit programs. |
| **Lay‑off notice or termination letter** | Shows you were let go through no fault of your own (UI requirement). |
| **Recent pay stubs or W‑2 forms** | Shows you earned enough wages for UI and helps determine training eligibility. |
| **Proof of residence** (utility bill, lease, or mail with your name) | Some county programs need to confirm you live in their area. |
| **Resume (if you have one)** | Helps staff give you targeted job‑search help. |
| **Bank account info** (for direct deposit of UI) | UI benefits are usually deposited directly into a bank account. |

---

## 5. Timelines to keep in mind  

| Action | Typical time frame |
|--------|--------------------|
| **File UI claim** | Should be done within 7 days of lay‑off. Benefits usually start within 2‑3 weeks after the claim is approved. |
| **CalJOBS registration** | Can be completed in 10‑15 minutes online. |
| **One‑Stop Center appointment** | Walk‑in may be available, but an appointment often gets you a quicker slot (same day or next day). |
| **WIOA training approval** | Usually 2‑4 weeks after you submit the application, but it varies by county. |
| **Medi‑Cal enrollment** | 30‑45 days from the date you submit the application, if you qualify. |
| **Weekly UI work‑search log** | Must be submitted **every week** while you receive UI. |

*These are general estimates. Your county’s office will give you the exact dates for your case.*

---

## 6. Other programs that might help (even if you didn’t ask)  

| Program | What it does | Who might need it |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| **SNAP (CalFresh)** | Food assistance for low‑income households. | If your income drops while you look for work. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage. | If you lose employer health insurance. |
| **CalWORKs** | Cash assistance for families with children who have very low income. | If you have kids and your income falls below the state limit. |
| **Apprenticeship Programs** (through the California Apprenticeship Initiative) | Paid on‑the‑job training in skilled trades. | Good if you want to learn

I’m really sorry you’re going through this. You don’t have to face it alone—there are people and programs that can help. Below is a simple guide to the main resources you can start with, what you’ll need, and how to get them.

---

## 1. Talk to Someone Right Now  
| What it is | How to reach it | What you’ll get |
|------------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Suicide & crisis helpline** (24‑hour, free) | Dial **988** (or 988‑555‑5555 if you need a TTY) | A caring counselor who can listen, give coping tips, and connect you to local help. |
| **California Mental Health Services** (county mental‑health department) | Call your county’s mental‑health line (look up “County Mental Health Services” on **2‑1‑1** or Google) | Free or low‑cost counseling, support groups, and sometimes medication assistance. |
| **2‑1‑1 California** (one‑stop info line) | Dial **2‑1‑1** or visit **211ca.org** | A friendly operator can tell you about food, housing, job training, and mental‑health services in your exact county. |

---

## 2. Money & Benefits While You Look for Work  

### a. Unemployment Insurance (UI)  
**What it is:** Weekly cash payments while you’re unemployed and looking for work.  
**Eligibility basics:**  
- You must have earned enough wages in the past 12‑month “base period.”  
- You must be able and available to work, and you must be actively looking for a job.  
**How to apply:**  
1. Go to **EDD.ca.gov** or call **1‑800‑300‑5616**.  
2. Create an online account (or use the phone system).  
3. Fill out the UI claim form and answer the work‑search questions each week.  
**Documents you’ll need:**  
- Your most recent pay stubs or W‑2s (to prove earnings).  
- Your driver’s license or ID number.  
- Your Social Security number.  
**Timeline:** First payment usually arrives 2‑3 weeks after you file, but you can get a “rapid‑response” payment if you’re in a disaster area or have a serious health issue.  

### b. CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids) – Cash Aid  
**What it is:** Monthly cash assistance for families with children who have low or no income.  
**Eligibility basics:**  
- You must live in California and have a child under 19 (or a disabled adult).  
- Income and assets must be below a set limit (the exact numbers change each year).  
- You must be willing to work, go to school, or take job‑training.  
**How to apply:**  
1. Contact your **County Human Services Agency (HSA)**. You can find the phone number on the **2‑1‑1** line.  
2. Fill out an application in person, online, or by mail.  
**Documents you’ll need:**  
- Proof of identity (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).  
- Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or mail addressed to you).  
- Recent pay stubs, bank statements, or a letter from your former employer showing your earnings.  
- Birth certificates for any children you’re adding.  
**Timeline:** After you submit a complete application, the county usually makes a decision within **30‑45 days**.  

### c. SNAP (CalFresh) – Food Benefits  
**What it is:** Monthly electronic benefits you can use to buy groceries.  
**Eligibility basics:**  
- Low household income (the exact limit varies by family size).  
- Must be a California resident.  
**How to apply:**  
1. Apply online at **GetCalFresh.org**, or call **1‑877‑847‑3663**.  
2. You can also apply in person at your county HSA.  
**Documents you’ll need:**  
- ID, proof of residence, and proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a letter from your former employer).  
- If you have a bank account, a recent statement.  
**Timeline:** Most people get a decision within **7‑10 days** and can start using benefits right away if approved.  

### d. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid) – Health Coverage  
**What it is:** Free or low‑cost health insurance for low‑income adults and families.  
**Eligibility basics:**  
- Income at or below about **138 % of the federal poverty level** (exact numbers change each year).  
- You must be a California resident.  
**How to apply:**  
1. Apply online at **CoveredCA.com** or call **1‑800‑541‑5555**.  
2. You can also apply at your county HSA.  
**Documents you’ll need:**  
- Same as for CalWORKs (ID, residence proof, income proof).  
**Timeline:** Usually a decision within **30 days**; coverage can start the first day of the month after approval.  

---

## 3. Job‑Search & Training Help  

| Program | Who it helps | What you get | How to start |
|---------|--------------|--------------|--------------|
| **CalJOBS** (state job board) | Anyone looking for work | Free job listings, resume help, workshops | Register at **caljobs.ca.gov** |
| **Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) – Adult Programs** | Adults (18‑64) who are unemployed or under‑employed | Free career counseling, job‑training vouchers, sometimes a stipend for training | Contact your local **American Job Center** (find one on **CalJOBS** or call **2‑1‑1**) |
| **Trade‑School & Apprenticeship Programs** | People who want hands‑on skills (construction, health care, tech, etc.) | Paid apprenticeships, on‑the‑job training, sometimes a stipend for tools or transportation | Ask the **American Job Center** or your county HSA for a list of approved programs. |
| **Rapid Re‑Hire (RRH) – for people who lost a job due to layoffs** | Workers who were laid off in the last 12 months | Short‑term cash assistance plus job‑placement services | Apply through your county HSA; they’ll tell you if RRH is available in your area. |

---

## 4. How to Keep Track of Everything  

1. **Make a simple checklist** (paper or phone note) with each program’s name, phone number, and what you still need to send.  
2. **Set a reminder** for each deadline (most programs give you 30‑45 days to submit documents).  
3. **Keep copies** of every form you send—digital PDFs are easiest to store.  

---

## 5. Remember: Rules Can Vary by County  

- **Eligibility limits, required documents, and processing times can be a little different** in each county.  
- The best way to know the exact details for you is to call **2‑1‑1** or your **County Human Services Agency**. They will tell you the local rules and can even help you fill out the forms.  

---

## 6. A Few Extra Resources You Might Find Helpful  

| Resource | What it offers | How to reach |
|----------|----------------|--------------|
| **California Department of Aging – Senior Services** | If you’re 60+ you can get extra food, transportation, and caregiver help. | Call **1‑800‑732‑2323** or visit **aging.ca.gov** |
| **Legal Aid Society of California** | Free legal help for issues like unemployment disputes, eviction, or benefits denials. | Find a local office at **lawhelpca.org** |
| **Community Action Agencies (CAAs)** | Local nonprofits that provide emergency cash, utility help, and sometimes job‑training vouchers. | Search “Community Action Agency + [your county]” or ask 2‑1‑1. |
| **Veterans Services** (if you served) | VA benefits, health care, and job‑placement programs. | Call **1‑800‑827‑1000** or visit **va.gov**. |
| **Housing Assistance (Section 8, Emergency Shelter)** | Help with rent or temporary shelter if you’re at risk of losing housing. | Contact your county HSA or 2‑1‑1. |

---

### Quick Steps to Get Started Today  

1. **Dial 988** if you feel you need immediate emotional support.  
2. **Call 2‑1‑1** (or go to 211ca.org) and ask for “unemployment, CalFresh, and mental‑health services in my county.” Write down the numbers they give you.  
3. **Apply for Unemployment Insurance** online at **EDD.ca.gov

## 1. Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)

**What it is** – Money that can be used to pay past‑due rent, future rent, or a combination of both.

**Who can apply**  
- You must live in California.  
- You must have a household income at or below about 80 % of the state median (the exact number changes each year, so the county will check the current limit).  
- You must be at risk of eviction or already have an eviction notice.

**How to apply**  
1. **Find your county’s portal** – Search “Emergency Rental Assistance [Your County]” or go to the California COVID‑19 ERA website and click “Apply Now.”  
2. **Create an account** and fill out the online form.  
3. **Upload required documents** (see list below).  
4. Submit and wait for a decision (usually 2‑4 weeks, but timing can vary by county).

**Documents you’ll need**  
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)  
- Proof of income (pay stubs, recent tax return, or unemployment claim receipt)  
- Lease or rental agreement  
- Recent rent bill or notice of past‑due rent  
- Eviction notice (if you have one)  
- Bank statement or proof of where you want the money sent

**What to expect**  
- If approved, the money is usually sent directly to your landlord.  
- You’ll get a letter confirming the amount and the date it will be paid.

---

## 2. Utility Assistance (CARES, LIHEAP, and County Programs)

**What it is** – Help paying electricity, gas, water, or phone bills when you can’t afford them.

**How to get it**  
1. **Call your utility company** – Ask for “payment assistance” or “hardship program.” Many utilities have their own emergency plans.  
2. **Apply for the California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE) program** – This gives a discount on your electric/gas bill if your income is low. You can apply online at the CARE website or by phone.  
3. **Apply for the Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)** – This is a federal program run by each county. Search “LIHEAP [Your County]” and follow the county’s online or phone application.  

**Typical documents**  
- Photo ID  
- Recent utility bill showing the amount owed  
- Proof of income (same as for rental assistance)  
- Lease or proof of residence  

**Timing** – CARE discounts are usually applied to your next bill. LIHEAP decisions can take 1‑3 weeks, depending on the county.

---

## 3. General Assistance / General Relief (County‑Level)

**What it is** – A cash benefit for adults who have no other income and are not eligible for CalWORKs.

**Who can apply** – Adults (18+) who are California residents, have very low or no income, and need help with basic needs like food, rent, or utilities.

**How to apply**  
- Contact your **County Human Services Agency** (often called “General Assistance” or “General Relief”).  
- You can usually apply in person, by phone, or sometimes online.  

**Documents** – Same basic set: ID, proof of income (or lack of income), lease, utility bills.

**Timeline** – Counties aim to decide within 30 days, but it can be faster if you have an urgent need.

---

| Step | What to Do | Why |
|------|------------|-----|

| 5 | **Start your unemployment claim** (if you haven’t already). Keep the claim receipt; it counts as proof of income for many programs. | You’ll need the receipt for assistance applications. |
| 6 | **Check your county’s General Assistance office** if you need extra cash after the above help. | Last‑resort safety net. |

---

## 5. A Note About County Differences

California runs these programs statewide, but each **county** decides how to process applications, what exact income limits they use, and how quickly they pay out. That means:

- The website you use, the phone number you call, and the paperwork checklist can look a little different from one county to another.  
- Some counties have “one‑stop” centers where you can apply for rental, utility, and cash assistance all at once. Others require separate applications.  

If you’re not sure which office to contact, search “County Human Services Agency + your county name” or call the **California Department of Social Services (CDSS) toll‑free at 1‑877‑847‑3663** for a quick direction.

---

- Write down the date you submit each application.  
- Note the reference number or case ID the agency gives you.  
- Follow up after the expected decision time (usually 2‑4 weeks for rental assistance, 1‑3 weeks for utility help).

It can feel overwhelming, but taking these steps one at a time will get you the help you need while your unemployment claim is processed. If you run into any roadblocks, call your county’s Human Services Agency—they’re there to help you navigate the process.

Take care, and good luck!

--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- Workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching.

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Below is a simple guide to help you understand how the food‑stamp program (called **CalFresh** in California) works, what can speed up the process, and how unemployment benefits, severance pay, or moving to another county might change things. I’ve also added a few other programs that could be useful.

---

## 1. CalFresh (Food Stamps) – the basics  

| What it is | A monthly benefit that lets you buy groceries. |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Who can apply | Anyone who lives in California, has a low or moderate income, and meets the citizenship/immigration rules. |
| Main eligibility factors | **Household size**, **income**, **resources (savings, bank accounts)**, and **any other benefits you already receive**. |
| Typical timeline | **First payment can arrive in as little as 7‑10 days** after you submit a complete application. Some counties can give a **“Rapid Response”** or **“Emergency”** allotment in 3‑5 days if you are in a crisis (no food, no money for a week, etc.). |

### How to apply quickly  

1. **Apply online** at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** – this is the fastest way.  
2. **Call your county’s CalFresh office** (the number is on the website) if you need help or want the emergency allotment.  
3. **Bring the required documents** (see below) to the office or upload them online.  
4. **Ask for “Rapid Response”** when you speak with a caseworker. Explain that you have no food and limited savings.

---

## 2. How UI (Unemployment Insurance) or severance pay affect CalFresh  

| Situation | Effect on CalFresh eligibility |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| **Receiving UI benefits** | UI counts as **income**. It is added to the household’s total when the county calculates whether you meet the income limit. It does **not** automatically disqualify you; many families get CalFresh while on UI. |
| **Receiving severance pay** | Severance is also counted as **income** in the month you receive it. If the amount is large, it could push your income above the limit for that month, but you can still qualify in later months once the severance is “used up.” |
| **Both UI and severance together** | The county adds them together with any other earnings. If the total is still under the limit for your household size, you remain eligible. If it’s over, you may get a reduced benefit or be placed on a “recertification” wait until your income drops. |

**Tip:** When you apply, tell the caseworker the exact amount of UI and any severance you expect. They can run the numbers and let you know what your benefit might look like.

---

## 3. Moving to another county (e.g., to live with your mom)  

* **You must re‑apply or update your address** with the new county’s CalFresh office.  
* **Eligibility rules are the same statewide**, but **each county processes applications at its own speed** and may have slightly different forms for “rapid response.”  
* If you move **before your first CalFresh payment arrives**, the original county will stop processing your case and the new county will start a new one. This can add a few extra days, but you can still ask for an emergency allotment in the new county.  
* **Living with your mom** may change your household size and income:  
  * If you **share a kitchen and meals**, you may be counted as part of your mom’s household (the county will decide based on who buys the food).  
  * If you keep your own food budget and pay your own share, you can stay a **separate household**. Tell the caseworker exactly how you plan to live so they can count the right household size.

---

## 4. What documents you’ll need  

| Document | Why it’s needed |
|----------|-----------------|
| **Proof of identity** – driver’s license, state ID, or passport. |
| **Proof of California residence** – utility bill, lease, or a letter from your mom if you move in with her. |
| **Social Security numbers** for everyone in the household. |
| **Proof of income** – recent UI award letter, recent pay stubs, severance check, or a letter from your former employer. |
| **Bank statements** (last 30 days) – to show savings/resources. |
| **Proof of expenses** (rent, utilities, child care) – helps the county see your net income. |
| **Child‑care or school enrollment paperwork** – if you have kids, this can affect the calculation. |

You can upload most of these online, or bring paper copies to the county office.

---

## 5. Quick step‑by‑step checklist  

1. **Go to GetCalFresh.org** and start an online application.  
2. **Select “Rapid Response/ Emergency”** when asked about your situation.  
3. **Gather the documents** listed above.  
4. **Submit the application** (online or in person).  
5. **Call the county office** (phone number on the site) to confirm they have everything and to ask about the emergency allotment.  
6. **If you move**, tell the new county as soon as you have a new address. They will start a new case; you can still request rapid response there.  
7. **Wait for a decision** – most counties respond within 7‑10 days; emergency cases can be approved in 3‑5 days.  
8. **If approved**, you’ll get an EBT card in the mail (usually within a week). Load it with your benefit amount and start buying groceries.

---

## 6. Other programs that might help right now  

| Program | What it does | Who can apply |
|---------|--------------|---------------|
| **CalWORKs** (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids) | Cash assistance for families with children, plus job‑training and child‑care help. | Low‑income families with kids; you may qualify even if you have some UI. |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | County‑level cash help for adults without other benefits. | Varies by county; often a “last‑resort” safety net. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage. | Most low‑income adults and children; automatic if you get CalFresh. |
| **WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)** | Nutrition vouchers for pregnant women, new moms, and kids up to age 5. | If you have a child under 5 or are pregnant. |
| **Rental Assistance (Section 8, COVID‑19 emergency funds, etc.)** | Helps pay rent or utility bills. | Income‑based; many counties have waiting lists. |
| **Job‑Search Services** (America’s Job Center of California) | Free help with resume, job listings, training, and sometimes transportation vouchers. | Anyone looking for work. |

You don’t have to apply for all of them, but checking a few can give you extra support while you look for a new job.

---

## 7. A few final reminders  

* **You are not automatically disqualified** because you receive UI or severance. Those amounts are just part of the income calculation.  
* **Moving does not end your benefits**, but you must tell the new county and may need to re‑apply.  
* **Emergency CalFresh** can give you food money in as little as a few days if you have no food at home.  
* **Each county processes things a little differently**, so timelines can vary. Call the local office if you feel things are taking too long.  

I hope this helps you get the food and other support you need while you look for a new job. If you have any more questions, just let me know!
